mechanism: Tranylcypromine (MAOI) inhibits monoamine oxidase, increasing serotonin levels, while oxycodone increases serotonin release, creating risk for serotonin syndrome; additionally, both drugs cause CNS depression with additive respiratory and hemodynamic effects.
action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, use lowest oxycodone dose with intensive monitoring for serotonin syndrome symptoms (agitation, hyperthermia, rigidity, hyperreflexia) and respiratory depression.
